studies.name: Devries et al. — Good School Toolkit RCT, Uganda (cited within Hunt et al. 2025 as the Uganda study with 3,820 participants)
studies.draft_uses: Described as 'an RCT with 3,820 participants of a school-wide intervention aiming to reduce violence from peers and staff toward students with and without disabilities'
studies.latest_known: Original RCT: Devries et al. 2015/2018, 42 schools, 3,820 students, Luwero District Uganda. A 2024 long-term follow-up (Knight et al., BMC Public Health 2024, Jun 7;24(1):1532) found no evidence of long-term effect on peer violence victimisation in later adolescence (aOR=0.81, 95%CI 0.59–1.11) in a non-randomised design. A November 2025 pilot RCT of a secondary-school adaptation (GST-S) was also published (BMC Public Health 25, 3802, 2025). The 3,820 participant figure and the original RCT framing remain accurate for the primary-school trial as cited.
studies.what_changed: The 3,820-participant figure and the original RCT description are confirmed correct. The 2024 long-term follow-up uses a different design (non-randomised), a different outcome (peer victimisation in later adolescence), and a different sample (adolescents followed up years later); it does not alter the figures the draft quotes from the original trial. The 2025 GST-S pilot is a separate secondary-school intervention and does not affect the draft's claim.
